cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Keeper! Welcome to the summit of the Meridian, the highest gate on the finest water road in the Vell. Here is the toll book. Guard it like a child.

left.label: Read it tonight
left.outcome: Eighty years of figures, in eleven hands.

right.label: Ask about the last Keeper
right.outcome: Pell's smile stays where it is. His eyes do not.

cards.notes: Always the first card of a run; forced by TurnController.begin_run.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A grain barge from Aldmere waits below the top gate. Papers in order, the bargee says, if you would care to look.

left.label: Check the papers
left.outcome: In order. The bargee spits, politely, over the side.

right.label: Open the gate
right.outcome: The paddles run, the chamber fills, the barge rises.

cards.speaker: mirren
cards.text: Mirren Dray. Lock hand. I turn the paddles, you decide when. That oilskin on the hook is not for anyone.

left.label: Leave it where it hangs
left.outcome: She nods once, which from her is a speech.

right.label: Ask whose it was
right.outcome: "His." She goes to the paddles.

cards.speaker: src_weather
cards.text: The sill gauge reads one mark lower than the last entry in the book. The reservoir report, pinned beside it, says nothing has changed.

left.label: Note it in the Ledger
left.outcome: A small line in a new hand.

right.label: A dry week, nothing more
right.outcome: The gauge does not argue.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Ilse Harrow. I keep the Wheel and Windlass and, when nobody else will, the town. A room is two marks a week. A welcome costs more.

left.label: Take the room
left.outcome: The bed is hard and the ale is good.

right.label: The Keeper's House will do
right.outcome: "It will. It did for him."

cards.speaker: src_telegram
cards.text: COMPANY TO KEEPER HALFWAY STOP REPORT TRAFFIC FIGURES EACH WATCH STOP DELAYS TO BE EXPLAINED STOP

left.label: Report exactly
left.outcome: Fennick taps it out with his tongue between his teeth.

right.label: Report weekly
right.outcome: Nobody wires back. Nobody wires back for three days.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: Sorry. Tamsin Quenn, engineer. The east lower paddle is roughly forty years past its work. I need eleven marks for a new spindle. I know it's your first day.

left.label: Approve the spindle
left.outcome: She is gone before you finish the signature.

right.label: Make it last a month
right.outcome: "It might. Roughly."

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A narrow boat of stitched sailcloth waits without a toll in hand. The woman at the tiller says the Hullfolk hold passage here, and always have.

left.label: Passage without fee
left.outcome: She does not thank you. She looks at you, which may be more.

right.label: The toll is the toll
right.outcome: She pays in old coin and remembers your face.

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: Odile Vosk, Summit Auditor. I have read your first entries. The hand is legible. You will find I read everything.

left.label: Then read this too
left.outcome: You hand her the page. She reads it. "Noted."

right.label: Ask what she is looking for
right.outcome: "Irregularities. For the record, there are none yet."

cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: Matthias Crane, Aldmere Customs, under the Halfway Compact of Year 58. I note that Schedule Four requires my seal on any arms. I will be here every watch.

left.label: Welcome his inspections
left.outcome: "Duly noted." He almost smiles, and files it.

right.label: Inspections slow the gate
right.outcome: "The Compact does not mention speed."

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: Nessa Vane, Sorrel Freight. Your predecessor cost my principals nine days last quarter. Here is the rate card. Here is the bill for the nine days.

left.label: The bill is not mine
left.outcome: "By the next watch it will be. We can fix that."

right.label: Promise faster passage
right.outcome: She writes it down before you have finished.

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: Fennick Orr, the wire. In strictest confidence, Keeper, you'll never guess what the last one wired the night before he went. I shouldn't. Shall I?

left.label: Tell me
left.outcome: "Three words. 'Found the key.' Then nothing."

right.label: Keep the wire's secrets
right.outcome: He looks at you as if you had refused a gift, then brightens.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A boat of grey-robed pilgrims asks to wait in the chamber while the chaplain blesses their hull. Two coal barges wait behind them.

left.label: Let the blessing finish
left.outcome: It takes a while. The coal barges say so.

right.label: Bless them on the towpath
right.outcome: The chaplain does not argue. She never does.

cards.speaker: bram
cards.text: We are Bram Holloway. We hold the Reed Reach. Every Keeper is one of two things, and the water finds out which. Are you a gate, or a wall?

left.label: A gate
left.outcome: "Then we shall see it open."

right.label: The Company's Keeper
right.outcome: "So was the last one. So was the first."

cards.speaker: wren
cards.text: Wren. I run things. Small favor: a crate goes down the east flight tonight and nobody writes it in the Book. Cargo. Nothing that bites.

left.label: Not in my Book
left.outcome: "Fair. I'll ask again when you're tired."

right.label: One crate
right.outcome: You didn't see it. A coin appears on the sill anyway.

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: Dray's chair. Dray's desk. Dray's study door, locked, with no key on the ring you were given.

left.label: Try the lock
left.outcome: It holds. Somebody meant it to.

right.label: Leave it for now
right.outcome: The chair, at least, is comfortable.

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: Sister Hale. We tend the Still Water chapel and bless what passes. The summit springs are a gift, Keeper. We do not ask the water where it comes from.

left.label: Accept the blessing
left.outcome: Her lamp swings over the gates. The hands take off their caps.

right.label: Ask where it comes from
right.outcome: "From the hill, as all still water does."

cards.speaker: solas
cards.text: Solas. Sorrel Escort Company. My convoys come through twice a month, armed and lawful. Tell me now how you want them handled. I would rather not learn it at the gate.

left.label: Inspected like any boat
left.outcome: "Understood. It won't come to trouble."

right.label: Escorts pass on sight
right.outcome: "My people will remember that."

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things, Keeper. The upper gate weeps. The hands are two short. And the last Keeper owed us a round he never stood.

left.label: Stand the round
left.outcome: Eleven tankards. Ilse counts them.

right.label: Fix the gate first
right.outcome: "Right. That's one of three."

cards.speaker: src_weather
cards.text: Rain all night. The pound is up a mark by morning and Ilse's cellar has an inch in it. She has sent a boy to say so.

left.label: Run the east paddles
left.outcome: Water goes down the flight. Boats wait while it does.

right.label: An inch is an inch
right.outcome: The boy goes back with nothing in his hands.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: A target, Keeper! Every magnificent enterprise needs one. Forty vessels a week through the top gate. The Meridian spirit demands no less.

left.label: Forty it is
left.outcome: He shakes your hand as if you had already done it.

right.label: Thirty, and safely
right.outcome: "Thirty. Well. A beginning."

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A Sorrel coal barge and an Aldmere grain boat arrive at the same bell. Both bargees are already shouting. The chamber holds one.

left.label: Grain first
left.outcome: Aldmere law says food before fuel. So does the grain boat.

right.label: Coal first
right.outcome: Sorrel's man tips his cap. Aldmere's writes something down.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The Company store sells beer at Company prices in Company scrip. Mine costs coin and tastes of something. Where does the Keeper drink?

left.label: The Wheel and Windlass
left.outcome: "Then you'll hear things. Some of them true."

right.label: The Company store
right.outcome: "Suit yourself. The scrip's no good here."

cards.speaker: src_telegram
cards.text: ALDMERE GUILDS TO KEEPER STOP GRAIN CONVOY NINE VESSELS ARRIVES TOMORROW STOP ANY DELAY WILL BE REPORTED UNDER THE COMPACT STOP

left.label: Clear the pound for them
left.outcome: Other boats are asked, then told, to wait.

right.label: They queue like anyone
right.outcome: Crane reads the wire twice and says nothing, loudly.

cards.speaker: mirren
cards.text: Did you open the study? You have the house. Nobody would say anything if you did.

left.label: It is locked, and I left it
left.outcome: "Good." Then, quieter: "For now."

right.label: I mean to
right.outcome: She looks at the door, then at you, then at the paddles.

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: Aurelie Stroud, physician. Dray kept every watch himself for a year. I have seen what that does. Sleep when the bell allows, or I will be seeing you.

left.label: Let Dace take a watch
left.outcome: You sleep. The gate does not fall down.

right.label: The gate needs a Keeper
right.outcome: "So did he."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: Watch six. Toll receipts exceed the book by two marks. Either a bargee overpaid, or something irregular. Which would you like it to be?

left.label: An overpayment; return it
left.outcome: "Noted. And the bargee's name?" You do not have it.

right.label: Into the repair fund
right.outcome: "For the record, that is not a fund."

cards.speaker: src_weather
cards.text: A dry week. The Cald Tarn aqueduct is a trickle you could step over. The pound, fed by it, is down only a mark. Somebody should find that strange.

left.label: Ask Quenn about it
left.outcome: "Sorry. Yes. It doesn't close. It never quite closes."

right.label: Be glad of it
right.outcome: The boats float. That is the Keeper's business.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A late boat, lamps out, asks passage after the last bell. The bargee is tired, he says. Dace, at the paddles, is looking at you.

left.label: Light your lamps and wait
left.outcome: He waits. He is not pleased. Dace is.

right.label: Pass him through
right.outcome: The chamber fills in the dark. Something shifts in his hold.

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: Eight watches. The book is in your hand now, and the town knows your face. You could write the first honest line about what kind of Keeper this will be.

left.label: The Company's, first
left.outcome: The line dries. It can be crossed out later, in theory.

right.label: The gate's, first
right.outcome: The Company does not read the Ledger. Yet.
